memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'I myself will set my face against him and will cut him off from his people; for by sacrificing his children to Molek, he has defiled my sanctuary and profaned my holy name. If the members of the community close their eyes when that man sacrifices one of his children to Molek and if they fail to put him to death, I myself will set my face against him and his family and will cut them off from their people together with all who follow him in prostituting themselves to Molek.'" - Lev 20:3-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at the phrase in verse 4: if the members of the community close their eyes.

God anticipates it. He knows that when something terrible happens, people find reasons not to see. It is a private family matter. It is not our business. Someone else will deal with it. And so a child dies while a whole village finds somewhere else to look.

God treats that silence as participation. The one who looked away is answerable too.

This is one of the most searching truths in Scripture. We tend to think of sin as things we do. God also names the things we allow — the harm we noticed and did not report, the pattern we suspected and did not question, the person we knew was in trouble and did not approach.

If you see something and say nothing, you have made a choice.

Rescue those being led away to death; hold back those staggering towards slaughter. If you say, "But we knew nothing about this," does not he who weighs the heart perceive it? (Prov 24:11-12).

There is grace for those who have failed here — but the first step is to stop closing our eyes.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something you have noticed and chosen not to see?
2. What makes it easier to look away than to speak up?
3. Who might be waiting for someone to finally say something?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the times I have looked away from what I should have seen. Give me courage to act rather than to find reasons for silence. Amen.
